publication.edition: Greek text with introduction and commentary; treatise conventionally dated 1st century CE

verification.verification_notes: Confirmed as a Roman-era Greek treatise of uncertain authorship ('Pseudo-Longinus'), with Russell 1964 as the standard Anglophone edition/commentary. Used for the theory that grandeur arises from elevated thought and figured composition that transports the hearer, and for cadence/amplification technique.

limitations: Claims about Greek rhythm and figures rest on the Greek; the tone card must not assert acoustic specifics from translation alone.

copyright.notes: Treatise public domain; Russell edition copyrighted; analytical citation only; no passages reproduced.
